title: Maximum Subarray
prompt:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray (at least one element).

**Example**: `[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4]` → `6` (subarray `[4,-1,2,1]`).

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ nums.length ≤ 10^5`, `-10^4 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^4`. Aim for O(n).

tests.note: all negative — must still take one element

hints: Suppose the best subarray ending at index i-1 has a negative sum. Would you ever attach it to nums[i]?
Keep `running` = the best sum of a subarray ending at the current index, and `best` = the largest `running` seen so far.
`running = Math.max(nums[i], running + nums[i])`. Seed both with `nums[0]`, not 0, or all-negative arrays break.

solution.explanation: `running` is the best sum of a subarray ending at i. A negative prefix only lowers any future sum, so dropping it (restarting at nums[i]) is always safe. Every subarray ends somewhere, so the max over all `running` values is the answer. O(n) time, O(1) space.
